answers.transcript:
Okay, I want to talk about one time I help a person that I don't know.
It was last year, in the winter.
I was waiting my bus in the bus station near my house and it was very cold.
There was an old woman with two big bags.
She want to go to the hospital but she don't know which bus she must take.
She ask me and first I don't understand because she speak very fast.
After I look in my phone and I find the number of the bus for the hospital.
I carry her bags to the bus and I say to the driver the name of the hospital.
She was very happy and she said thank you many times.
After this I feel very good, all the day I am in a good mood.
It was only five minutes, but for her it was important.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The event is told from start to finish and the sequence can be followed, but each step is a single sentence and transitions are made with after / and. The card's final point (how she felt afterwards) is closed in two sentences.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The narrative runs on the everyday core: very cold, very happy, very good, big bags. The only expression describing the help is "I carry her bags"; there is no collocation of the kind the card suggests.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The narrative starts in the past but slips into the present in most places (she want, she don't know, I look, I find, I carry, I feel), and there are dropped prepositions (waiting my bus). Structures are simple sentences; there is one which clause.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Pull the whole narrative into the past tense — the story is soundly built, the only thing spoiling it is the tense shift. Then open up the final point: say what was actually thought that day instead of "very good".

answers.transcript:
I'd like to talk about a time when I helped an old lady at the bus station, it was maybe one year ago in winter.
I was going to my cousin's house and I was waiting for my bus, and it was really cold that evening, so everybody was standing close to the wall.
Then I noticed an old woman with two big bags. She was looking at the timetable and after that at the buses, and it was clear that she was lost.
She asked me something but at the beginning I didn't understand her, because she was speaking very fast and with a strong accent.
After a moment I understood that she needed to go to the state hospital and she didn't know which bus goes there.
So I looked on my phone, I found the number, and I said her to wait with me, because the bus was coming after seven minutes.
When it came I helped her with the bags and I explained to the driver where she wants to get off.
Honestly, it took me five minutes, nothing more. But she thanked me so much that I felt a little bit ashamed, and for all the day I was in a good mood.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The event develops scene by scene (waiting, noticing, not understanding, the solution) and the listener is never lost anywhere. Transitions are orderly with then / after that / so but monotonous; the change of tone in the closing with "Honestly, it took me five minutes" is good.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is vocabulary to build the scene (timetable, strong accent, lost, ashamed, in a good mood), and meaning is clear throughout. Choice slips in two places: "for all the day", "the bus was coming after seven minutes".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The past continuous, reported speech and that clauses are controlled; two-thirds of sentences are error-free. The remaining errors are specific: verb pattern (I said her to wait), tense agreement in reported speech (where she wants to get off), preposition (after seven minutes).

answers.what_would_lift_it: Take the closing a little further: the sentence describing the feeling of embarrassment is the response's most interesting part but stays in a single sentence. In the language, fix the said her / told her distinction.

answers.transcript:
This happened about a year ago, at the bus station near my flat, one of those freezing winter evenings where everyone's huddled up against the wall pretending they're not cold.
I was waiting for a bus over to my cousin's place and I noticed an elderly woman with two enormous shopping bags. She kept looking up at the timetable and then back at the buses, and she just looked a bit lost, so I asked her if she was all right.
It took me a minute to work out what she needed, to be honest. She was speaking very quickly and she had quite a strong regional accent. But eventually I got that she was trying to reach the state hospital and she had no idea which bus went there. Nobody else had stopped, by the way, although half the queue must have heard her.
So I looked it up on my phone, found out it was the number twelve, and told her to wait with me.
When it turned up I gave her a hand with the bags and had a quick word with the driver so he'd tell her when to get off.
It can't have taken more than five minutes, but she was so grateful that I felt slightly embarrassed, actually.
And I'll admit it put me in a good mood for the rest of the evening, which probably says more about me than it does about her.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative is fluent and detailed; the scene is built in a single sentence ("everyone's huddled up against the wall pretending they're not cold") and stands developed with side notes such as "Nobody else had stopped, by the way". The closing turns the narrative back on itself and ties it together.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Idiomatic items are plentiful and in place: huddled up, looked a bit lost, work out, had no idea, turned up, gave her a hand with, had a quick word with, put me in a good mood, half the queue. The register is spoken throughout.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is wide: the past perfect (Nobody else had stopped), an inference structure (can't have taken), so + purpose, reported speech. Errors are rare; "I got that she was trying to reach" is natural in speech and costs the listener nothing.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target. For the next level up, the observation that nobody else had stopped needs to be run one sentence further; at present it is left as an interesting detail.
